title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a space (scheme or topos) and k is a sheaf of rings on it. A^{**} is an object of DR_sp(X,k), which this page calls a 'special De Rham bialgebra'. It is bigraded, with A^{00}=k and A^{0j}=0 for j>0. In the staircase diagram, A^{ij} vanishes unless j ≤ i. The second index is the 'cotangent degree'; the first is the total degree, so i−j is the 'complementary degree'. The vertical differential is d: A^{ij} → A^{i,j+1}, giving the columns A^{10}→A^{11} and A^{20}→A^{21}→A^{22}.

Step 1: the extension. A global section T of A^{10} defines k → Φ := A^{10}, λ ↦ λT. One gets an exact sequence 0 → k → Φ → Ψ → 0. Logically Ψ is identified, via d, with A^{11}; the arrow under Ψ in the image points to an A^{?0}/A^{11} term.

Step 2: the model object. Since Ψ is k-flat, Φ is flat too. One forms DR(Φ,T) = Γ^*(Φ) ⊗_k Λ^*Ψ:
- Γ^a(Φ) sits in complementary degree a and Λ^bΨ in cotangent degree b, so DR(Φ,T)^{ij} = Γ^{i−j}(Φ) ⊗ Λ^jΨ.
- The differential is d(x^{[n]}) = x^{[n−1]}·dx, where dx is the image of x in Ψ; it is extended as a derivation.
- In modern terms, this is the divided-power de Rham complex of the PD polynomial algebra Γ_k(Φ) relative to the PD subalgebra Γ_k(kT). Its Ω^1 is Γ(Φ)⊗Ψ because Ψ = Φ/kT.
- Locally Φ ≅ k⊕Ψ. Then DR(Φ,T) ≅ Γ(kT) ⊗ (Γ(Ψ)⊗ΛΨ), the second factor being the PD Koszul/de Rham complex of Ψ. By the PD Poincaré lemma it resolves Γ_k(kT) in all characteristics.
- The text asserts that DR(Φ,T), with its bidifferential structure, is itself a special De Rham bialgebra.

Step 3: universality. By the universal property of Γ (divided powers) and of Λ, there is a canonical bialgebra map DR(Φ,T) → A^{**}. It is functorial: a morphism A^{**} → A'^{**} gives a commutative square with DR(Φ',T') → A'^{**}.

Step 4: the conclusion. The full subcategory DR_sp(X,k)_0 is presumably the special DR bialgebras for which this canonical map is an isomorphism (those 'generated in degree 1'). It is canonically equivalent to the category of algebras of the form DR(Φ,T). That in turn is equivalent to the category of extensions 0 → k → Φ → Ψ → 0 with Ψ flat over k.

Purpose. This is part of the 1976 IHÉS lecture material on the divided-power De Rham complex. It classifies the 'linear' or 'free' special DR bialgebras by extension data (Φ,T), a first step toward describing general special DR bialgebras.

Page context. The neighbouring pages are typescript pages of SGA 7 exposé IX (Néron models, monodromy pairing), reused as scrap paper. They are unrelated to the content of this page.
errors: The source of T is not specified: for the functoriality square with T' to make sense, T must be part of the structure of a special DR bialgebra (e.g. a distinguished primitive or unit section of A^{10}), or be canonically determined by it. As written, 'T ∈ Γ_X(A^{10})' looks like an arbitrary choice.
Exactness of 0→k→Φ→Ψ→0 (injectivity of λ↦λT, and the identification Ψ ≅ A^{11} via d) is assumed, not derived. Presumably it is an axiom of 'spéciale'.

The subcategory DR_sp(X,k)_0 is not defined on this page. The equivalence claim is only sketched ('aisément'): essential surjectivity and full faithfulness are not checked, and neither is the compatibility of the coalgebra structure with the extension data.

ideas.what: Bigraded divided-power de Rham algebra DR(Φ,T)=Γ(Φ)⊗ΛΨ attached to an extension 0→k→Φ→Ψ→0, i.e. the PD de Rham complex of Γ(Φ) relative to Γ(kT)
ideas.modern_name: PD (divided power) de Rham / de Rham–Koszul complex of a PD polynomial algebra
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture notes (this archive cote)

ideas.what: Universal property: canonical bialgebra map DR(Φ,T) → A^{**} for any special De Rham bialgebra, functorial in A
ideas.modern_name: Free / initial object generated in degree 1 for bigraded PD dg-bialgebras

ideas.what: Equivalence between the subcategory DR_sp(X,k)_0 and the category of extensions of a flat module Ψ by k (pairs (Φ,T) with Φ/kT flat)
ideas.modern_name: Classification of 'linear' Hodge-filtered PD de Rham bialgebras by extension data

missed.claim: Grothendieck introduces an axiomatic category DR_sp(X,k) of 'special De Rham bialgebras' (bigraded, with complementary and cotangent degrees, PD structure, and a Hopf structure). He classifies its 'degree-1 generated' part by extensions 0→k→Φ→Ψ→0. No published theory of such bigraded PD de Rham bialgebras with this classification seems to exist. The general (non-free) objects are left untreated here.
missed.quote: la cat. des DR_sp(X,k)_0 est équivalente canoniquement : à la catégorie ... déduite des algèbres de la forme DR(Φ,T), qui est aussi celle des suites exactes 0 → k → Φ → Ψ → 0 avec Ψ plat sur k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bigraded PD de Rham objects carrying a Hopf structure and an extension class resemble current stacky approaches to Hodge-filtered de Rham cohomology (G_a^♯, filtered de Rham stacks of Drinfeld and Bhatt–Lurie). An axiomatisation from 1976 could be historically interesting, but the link is speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page (PD de Rham complex of a divided-power polynomial algebra and its universal property) is standard. The only notable features are the unpublished axiomatic notion of 'special De Rham bialgebra' and its classification by extensions, which document the content of the lost 1976 IHÉS lecture, though they are not a striking new result.
transcription_corrections: Under Ψ in the exact sequence the vertical arrow should, logically, be an identification of Ψ with A^{11} (via d), not 'Ψ → A^{20}'. The image is ambiguous ('A^{?0}').
'muni des [-structures-] bi-différentielles' likely reads 'muni des structures bi-différentielles' with an inserted correction; the struck word is uncertain.
'est une bi-alg. de De Rham spéciale' and 'un k-hom canonique de bialgèbres' are plausible readings of the abbreviated script.
'Cela [-implique-] signifie aisément': the image may instead read 'Cela implique aisément', with the strike-through on another word. Uncertain.
The prior and next pages are SGA 7 exposé IX typescript pages (scrap paper), not part of this manuscript's argument.
